Thanks Elena — this is exactly the kind of input we want before locking the SOW. High level answers below; Karthik and Marcus, I’m looping you in for the billing and technical implications.

TL;DR: We support both a global committed pool and region-specific allocation. Which is best depends on: (a) whether you need separate invoices/ledgers per region, (b) data residency/egress constraints, and (c) tolerance for transient tier behavior (i.e., filling/emptying a tier from bursts in one region).

Options we typically propose:
- Global pooled commit: single pool of tokens, single invoice. Best for customers who want simplicity and to maximize blended discounts.
- Region-tagged commit with blended tiers: commit is reserved centrally but discounts are calculated per-region then blended monthly — useful if you need regional cost visibility.
- Dedicated regional commits: separate commit for each region, separate invoices. Useful for regulatory or chargeback needs.

Elena — can you confirm whether Procurement needs separate invoices per legal entity/region? If not, global pooled commit will likely give Orion the best economics.

Mina/Eleanor (cc’ed as Elena),

Quick technical/billing primer to make this concrete:

1) Billing model: commit tiers are applied per invoice period (monthly by default). By default we deduct all usage from a single committed pool (global). Discounts apply based on the monthly aggregated token consumption against committed thresholds.

2) Region routing: we route requests based on the routing policy in the customer config. If you route APAC traffic to a US host, the tokens are still counted as usage under your global commitment — there is no additional per-token surcharge for cross-region routing by default. However:
  - Egress & compliance: if you require APAC data to remain in-region (data residency) we will not route out-of-region without an explicit config and contractual agreement.
  - Latency & QoS: routing APAC->US may increase latency and could push more requests into fallbacks (affects perceived reliability).

3) Region-aware discounts: we can also enable "region-aware" accounting where discounts are computed per-region if you want to guarantee that EU/APAC usage doesn't drive a single region's cliffing behavior. We then produce a blended report monthly so you can see the effective blended unit price. This mode is helpful when customers have separate cost centers per region.

4) Practical recommendation for Orion's scenarios:
  - If you want a single P&L and fastest procurement, pick Global pooled commit (single invoice).
  - If legal/finance needs separate invoices, go Region-tagged commit and we can set up per-region sub-commit balances (this will slightly reduce the overall blended discount compared to pooling).

I’ll produce a worked example (numbers) in the next message — Marcus, I left the sample spreadsheet with the scenarios attached for you to chase the math.

Elena / team — I ran the three scenarios from your spreadsheet through our pricing model. Summary below (numbers rounded):

Scenario A: 60% US / 30% EU / 10% APAC monthly volume (~9B tokens/month)
- Global pooled commit (1 contract): effective unit price = $0.00135/token; monthly commitment needed for Tier 2 discount = 7.5B tokens
- Region-tagged (separate buckets): blended effective = $0.00145/token (because APAC volume ends up in a smaller APAC bucket and hits a lower discount tier)
- Routing APAC->US with global pool: cost ~ same as global pooled commit; watch latency tradeoffs.

Scenario B: APAC-heavy bursty (40% APAC sustained with 2x peak bursts)
- Global pool: bursts help you climb tiers faster so your effective blended price improves across month; downside — if bursts are concentrated at month end you could see unpredictable tier cliffs for engineering.
- Dedicated APAC commit: smoother predictability but worse blended unit economics unless you commit larger APAC volumes.

Practical suggestion: For Orion I recommend Global pooled commit with a small per-region visibility split (we produce a monthly export that shows per-region consumption and effective unit price). If governance requires separate accounting, use region-tagged commits for EU + APAC and keep US on global pool — that hybrid avoids paying APAC-specific discounts while still letting US volume drive large-tier benefits.

I attached a one-page excel tab with a worked example and a short sensitivity chart. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the numbers.
